metaDesc: Compare 4 well-reviewed Thai cooking classes in Krabi-Ao Nang, from a chef's school running since 1995 to a class where you pick 15+ dishes yourself. ogTitle: Krabi Cooking Classes Compared — Which One Fits You
ogDesc: A legendary chef's school in Ao Nang · small classes with close attention · pick from 15+ dishes yourself, vegetarian-friendly too — compare market tours, dish counts, and prices from real reviews
heroCredit: Photo: Thai Secret Cooking School · CC BY-SA 4.0
intro: Krabi and Ao Nang have plenty of Thai cooking classes to choose from, and almost all of them sell a similar pitch: "market walk + cook it yourself + eat what you made." But once you look closer, the details vary quite a bit. Some are run by a chef's school that's been teaching since 1995 and has become a neighborhood legend. Some keep classes small so everyone gets proper attention. And some let you pick your own dishes from a list of 15 or more, with vegetarian options available too. We compared 4 well-reviewed classes that genuinely operate in Krabi-Ao Nang, and tell you straight who each one suits best — whether a market tour is included, how many dishes you'll make, what time slots are offered, and roughly how much it costs — so you can pick the class that fits your style without having to guess

blocks.html:
A cooking class is an activity that visitors to Krabi love to slot into half a day, because it gives you a break from the beach itinerary while also letting you take home the ability to actually cook Thai food. Most classes run for about 3-4 hours, starting with a walk through a fresh market to get familiar with vegetables, curry pastes, and ingredients you can't find back home. Then it's back into the kitchen to cook dish by dish at your own station, wrapping up with sitting down to eat what you made and taking the recipes home with you.

But the details are what set each class apart — for example, whether a market tour is included in the price or you're simply dropped off at a night market after the class, how much say you get in choosing your own dishes, whether they take small groups or large ones, and whether they can genuinely adapt recipes for vegetarians rather than just swapping meat for tofu. This article compares them clearly so you can see what each class does best, so you spend your money on the experience that actually matches what you're after

blocks.descHtml:
Krabi Thai Cookery School is a cooking school run by Chef "Ya" (Cholaya Laothong), tucked away in a garden-house neighborhood behind the bustle of Ao Nang. It's been teaching since 1995, making it one of the first names that comes to mind when people talk about cooking classes in Krabi. The class is held in an open-sided pavilion beside the chef's home, overlooking a small stream and surrounded by tropical garden. Each student gets their own cooking station. The class starts with a walk through a fresh market to get to know the ingredients, then it's back into the kitchen to cook 4 dishes chosen from a list of around 9 — things like spring rolls, curries, soups, stir-fries — finishing with mango sticky rice

Genuine reviews on Tripadvisor are almost unanimous in praising Chef Ya as kind, patient, and genuinely deeply knowledgeable about Thai food. Many say the small group size means you get close, personal guidance, the food is delicious enough to eat until you're full, and you get a recipe booklet with explanations of Thai ingredients to take home. What makes this place special in many people's eyes is that Chef Ya once taught Gordon Ramsay how to make som tam on his TV show, which only underscores that she's a genuine teacher, not just someone running classes for tourists

Something worth knowing before booking: there are both afternoon and evening slots. Some reviews mention the evening slot tends to be busier, so if you want a slower pace with more one-on-one time, choose the afternoon slot. And because this is a well-known school with limited capacity per slot, you should book ahead, especially during high season. One more thing — the location is in a garden-house neighborhood behind Ao Nang, so confirm the meeting point and transport arrangements clearly before class day
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: If you want an unhurried atmosphere with close attention from the teacher, choose the afternoon slot rather than the evening one, which tends to be busier. And if you can't handle spicy food or are vegetarian, let them know when booking so the chef can adjust the menu accordingly

blocks.descHtml:
Smart Cook Thai Cookery School is a class in Ao Nang with a high Tripadvisor score (around 4.8 from several hundred reviews). Its clear selling point is keeping classes small, taking a maximum of around 10 people per session, so the chef can give everyone close attention and personal guidance. The class runs about 4 hours, starting with a walk through a fresh market to get to know Thai ingredients and curry pastes, with a guide who explains things in a friendly, fun way. Then it's back into the kitchen to cook dish by dish through to dessert. Afterward you sit down to eat what you made and take home a certificate along with a recipe booklet

Genuine reviews praise the chef for teaching in an easy-to-understand way, focusing on explaining how to balance flavors in Thai food — the key skill that beginners often get wrong. Many say the market walk is the highlight that helps them understand the ingredients better, and because the group is small, no one feels rushed or has to fight over a stove. Most packages include hotel pickup within the Ao Nang area, which is convenient for anyone without their own transport

Worth knowing: because this is a small class with great reviews, spots per session fill up fast, so book ahead, especially in high season. Also check before booking whether your chosen slot includes both the market tour and hotel pickup, as details can vary by package. If you're vegetarian or have allergies, let them know when booking so the chef can prepare enough ingredients
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: If you want a class where the chef gives close attention and you never feel rushed, choose this one since groups are capped at around 10 people — and confirm before booking that your chosen slot includes both the market tour and hotel pickup within the Ao Nang area

blocks.descHtml:
Thai Charm Cooking School is a class with a very high Tripadvisor score (around 4.9 from several hundred reviews). What sets it apart from the others is the freedom to choose your own menu — here you can pick up to 5 savory dishes plus 2 desserts from a list of over 15, ranging from tom yum goong, tom kha gai, pad Thai, and chicken with cashew nuts, to various curries. Importantly, every dish can be made vegetarian, vegan, spicy or not spicy as you like, which makes it a great fit for groups with different dietary preferences on the same trip. There's pickup from Ao Nang or Krabi Town to the school, and the chef guides you through everything from pounding your own curry paste to techniques for cooking jasmine rice and sticky rice

Genuine reviews particularly praise Chef Penny for being welcoming, teaching in a fun way, and making the whole class feel warm and friendly — many say this is what made the experience five-star. The format has you cooking every dish yourself, which suits anyone who wants to actually be able to recreate it back home. And because you choose your own menu, you get to cook what you actually want to eat, rather than a fixed set. After class, you can also opt to be dropped off at the Krabi night market to keep exploring

Worth knowing: this class focuses more on kitchen cooking and menu choice than on an early-morning fresh market walk like some other schools. If you want the full fresh-market ingredient-picking experience, ask the organizer beforehand whether your booked slot includes a market segment. And because reviews are so good, slots fill up fast — book ahead, especially for the popular evening slot
blocks.tipHtml: Tip: If you're vegetarian, vegan, or your group has different dietary needs, choose this one since every dish can be adapted — and plan out which dishes you actually want to cook from the list of 15+ in advance to make the most of your time

blocks.descHtml:
Penny Thai Cookery School is a Krabi class that focuses on fun and being easy to follow, suited to beginners who've never cooked Thai food before. It's a half-day, hands-on class where the chef guides you through 5 savory Thai dishes plus 1 dessert such as mango sticky rice. It starts with the basics of pounding curry paste and seasoning, then you cook dish by dish until you're full from your own cooking. It's located in an easily accessible area, and after class you can also opt for a drop-off at the Krabi night market to explore and grab snacks

What reviewers mention most is the friendly class atmosphere and the kind teacher, which makes people who are worried they can't cook actually enjoy themselves and follow along successfully. The dishes taught are popular, familiar Thai favorites like pad Thai, tom yum, and curries, so they're not hard to recreate at home. The starting price is more accessible than premium classes, making it a good value option for anyone wanting to try a cooking class for the first time without paying a lot

Worth knowing: this class focuses on kitchen cooking and a night-market drop-off afterward, rather than an early-morning fresh market ingredient-picking walk. If you want the full fresh market experience, ask the organizer beforehand whether your booked slot includes one, and confirm pickup arrangements and the meeting point clearly, as details can vary by package and time slot

blocks.title: How to choose a genuine Krabi cooking class
blocks.html:
First, check what kind of market tour is included, since many reviews say the early-morning fresh market walk is the highlight — you get to know vegetables, curry pastes, and ingredients you can't find back home. But some classes in Krabi are a "drop-off at the night market after class" format, which is not the same thing as a fresh market tour where you pick ingredients yourself. If you want the ingredient-picking walk, choose a class that clearly states it includes a fresh market tour

Second, check the group size and menu choice. A small class like Smart Cook lets the chef give close attention without everyone fighting over a stove, while a class that lets you choose a lot of your own dishes, like Thai Charm, suits people who want to cook specific dishes or groups with different diets. Try reading reviews to see which type it is before booking

Third, disclose any dietary restrictions when you book. If you're vegetarian or vegan, choose a class that can adapt every dish, so you get food that's genuinely adjusted for you rather than just having vegetables swapped in for meat. And finally, confirm the pickup point and contact number, since many schools are located in garden neighborhoods or outside the town center — there have been reviews mentioning pickup vehicles not arriving as arranged. Confirming the night before class helps avoid that kind of mishap

faq.q: Which Krabi cooking classes include a fresh market walk
faq.a: Krabi Thai Cookery School (Chef Ya's) and Smart Cook both include a fresh market tour where you walk and pick ingredients before cooking. Thai Charm and Penny focus more on kitchen cooking and instead offer a drop-off at the night market after class. If you want to walk through a fresh market and pick your own ingredients, choose a package that specifically states it includes a fresh market tour before booking

faq.q: How much do Krabi cooking classes cost
faq.a: Most run around ฿1,000–1,800 per person for a half-day class that includes ingredients and a meal you cook yourself. Chef Ya's school runs around ฿1,500–1,700. Compare whether the market tour and hotel pickup are included, not just the number itself

faq.q: Are there Krabi cooking classes suitable for vegetarians or vegans
faq.a: Yes — Thai Charm Cooking School is known for being able to adapt every dish to vegetarian, vegan, spicy or not spicy as needed. Other schools can also adjust for vegetarian dishes. It's recommended to disclose any dietary restrictions when booking so the chef can prepare enough ingredients

faq.q: How long do Krabi cooking classes take, and are they suitable for beginners
faq.a: Most are half-day classes running about 3-4 hours, with both afternoon and evening slots. They suit beginners well, since the chef teaches step by step starting from pounding curry paste and seasoning. Many reviews from people who'd never cooked Thai food before say they were able to recreate the dishes at home afterward. If you want an unhurried pace, choose a small-group class or the afternoon slot

faq.q: Should you book Krabi cooking classes in advance
faq.a: Yes, you should book ahead, especially for well-reviewed schools like Chef Ya's, Smart Cook, and Thai Charm, which have limited capacity per slot and fill up fast during high season. Booking ahead also gives you time to disclose dietary restrictions and confirm pickup arrangements before class day
